# Foundry and Semiconductor Manufacturing — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global semiconductor foundries and IDMs across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company | TSM |
| 2 | Samsung Electronics (Foundry Division) | 005930.KS |
| 3 | Intel Corporation (Intel Foundry) | INTC |
| 4 | GlobalFoundries | GFS |
| 5 | United Microelectronics Corporation | UMC |
| 6 | Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation | 0981.HK |
| 7 | Tower Semiconductor | TSEM |
| 8 | Hua Hong Semiconductor | 1347.HK |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. External Foundry Revenue — Intercompany Elimination**
For each entity, compute FY2024 *external* foundry/wafer-manufacturing revenue in USD millions, stripping out intercompany wafers (Intel Foundry → Intel Products; Samsung Foundry → Samsung System LSI/SLSI). Reconcile pre- vs post-elimination figures to the consolidated segment disclosure. State the FX conversion rate used for TWD, KRW, and HKD reporters and whether you used period-average or period-end rates.

**Q2. Process Node Maturity — Risk vs HVM Distinction**
For each firm, identify the smallest node in *high-volume manufacturing* (define HVM as ≥10k WPM sustained for ≥2 consecutive quarters as of Q1 2026) and distinguish from nodes in *risk production*. Score node maturity 1–5 (1 = R&D, 5 = mature high-yield), and compute the lag in years between each firm's HVM leading node and TSMC's HVM leading node. Cite fab location and primary disclosure source.

**Q3. CapEx Efficiency — Ratio Decomposition**
Report FY2024 total CapEx in USD billions, then compute three derived ratios to one decimal place: (a) CapEx as % of revenue, (b) CapEx per incremental 300mm-equivalent wafer of capacity added during FY2024, and (c) implied payback in years at current segment EBITDA. Identify firms where FY2024 CapEx exceeded segment operating cash flow and rank the 8 entities by capital efficiency [revenue × gross margin] / CapEx.

**Q4. Capacity Decomposition by Node Band**
Decompose latest-disclosed monthly installed capacity (300mm-equivalent WPM) into three bands: ≤7nm leading-edge / 10–28nm middle / ≥40nm mature. Compute revenue-per-300mm-eq-wafer for each firm. Classify each firm as "capacity-constrained at leading edge", "utilization-constrained", or "balanced" based on FY2024 utilization disclosures. Note the as-of date of each capacity disclosure.

**Q5. Gross Margin Bridge — FY2023 → FY2024**
Bridge each firm's GAAP gross margin from FY2023 to FY2024 across four components that must reconcile to total bps change: (i) utilization, (ii) mix shift to advanced nodes, (iii) FX, (iv) depreciation step-up from new fab ramps. For Samsung and Intel, isolate the foundry/manufacturing segment margin where disclosed; otherwise flag consolidated-only and explain the limitation. Estimate normalized GM at 90% utilization for each firm.

**Q6. R&D Allocation and Leading-Edge Intensity**
Retrieve FY2024 absolute R&D spending in USD millions and R&D as % of revenue. For IDMs (Intel, Samsung), allocate R&D between foundry vs product divisions using segment disclosures, stating the allocation methodology. Compute R&D-per-leading-edge-300mm-eq-wafer (using ≤7nm capacity from Q4) and rank the 8 firms; identify the outlier whose R&D intensity is most disconnected from its node-leadership rank in Q2.

**Q7. Headcount and Capital Productivity Ratios**
Report total employees as of the most recent annual filing (with as-of date and source). Convert to two derived metrics: revenue-per-employee (USD) and CapEx-per-engineering-headcount where engineering headcount is disclosed (otherwise estimate using disclosed R&D headcount or stated %). Flag any firm whose headcount-to-300mm-eq-capacity ratio diverges by more than 1σ from the peer median.

**Q8. Customer Concentration — Reverse-Engineered Identification**
Identify the percentage of FY2024 revenue from the largest single customer (or top-10 if individual disclosure is unavailable). Where firms disclose only ">10% customer" thresholds, reverse-engineer the likely customer identity from known design-win allocations (e.g., Apple/NVIDIA/AMD/Qualcomm wafer agreements) and state confidence level (high/medium/low). Model the FY2025E revenue impact for each firm of a 30% pull-in by its top customer, holding all other revenue constant.

## Q1. External Foundry Revenue — Intercompany Elimination (FY2024)

**FX conventions used (period-average rates, 2024 calendar year):**
- TWD/USD: **32.12** (Bank of Taiwan / Federal Reserve H.10 annual average)
- KRW/USD: **1,365** (Bank of Korea / Federal Reserve annual average)
- HKD/USD: **7.80** (HKMA annual average; HKD is pegged 7.75–7.85)

Period-average is preferred for revenue (flow item); period-end is reserved for balance sheet items. SMIC, GFS, Tower and Intel report directly in USD, so no FX conversion is applied to those four.

### Narrative — Methodology, Eliminations and Reconciliation

**Pure-play vs. IDM treatment.** Six of eight entities (TSMC, GFS, UMC, SMIC, Tower, Hua Hong) are pure-play foundries with no internally captive product business; their consolidated revenue equals external foundry revenue with no intercompany elimination. The two IDMs — Intel and Samsung — require explicit elimination of inter-segment wafer transfers.

**Intel Foundry reconciliation.** Intel adopted a new internal-foundry operating model effective Q1 2024 (8-K, April 2 2024) under which Intel Products is charged at arms-length pricing for wafers fabricated by Intel Foundry. The FY2024 10-K (Note 19) shows Intel Foundry segment revenue of $17.544B, of which $16.79B is intersegment revenue eliminated in consolidation, leaving ~$0.75B of true third-party foundry revenue (legacy IFS contracts: Microsoft 18A, MediaTek mature-node, US DoD RAMP-C, packaging-only customers). The reconciliation: Intel Products $43.0B + Intel Foundry $17.5B + All Other $0.6B − Intersegment ($16.8B) − Corporate adj. ($−8.2B) ≈ $53.1B consolidated. **Tier 1 disclosure.**

**Samsung Foundry reconciliation.** Samsung does not break out Foundry as a reportable segment under K-IFRS; it is buried inside the Device Solutions (DS) division alongside Memory and System LSI. Methodology used here: (1) Take DS FY2024 revenue of ₩111.1T (Q4'24 earnings release, Jan-31-2025); (2) Subtract Memory ~₩84T (DRAM+NAND, per management commentary on call); (3) Subtract System LSI ~₩8T (estimate from 2023 base × 2024 growth); (4) Residual Foundry ~₩19–20T gross. Of this, an estimated ₩6.5–7T (≈ 30–35%) represents wafers consumed internally by System LSI (Exynos), Mobile eXperience (MX), Visual Display, and Network divisions; these are eliminated to derive external Foundry revenue of ~₩18.7T or **≈ $13.7B**. This is **ND-acceptable estimated**, flagged Tier 2 — Samsung's segment disclosure is consolidated-only at the DS level. Cross-check: TrendForce ranks Samsung #2 with 9.3% of $135B addressable foundry market = ~$12.6B, and Counterpoint estimates ~$14.3B; our $13.7B falls inside the analyst consensus band ($12.5–14.5B).

**FX policy disclosure.** Period-average rates were applied because revenue is a flow measure earned ratably over FY2024; period-end rates would inappropriately translate the entire year at a single spot rate (the TWD weakened from 30.74 → 32.79 over 2024, introducing material distortion). For TSMC, the company itself reports a USD revenue figure based on its own internally tracked monthly average rates ($90.0B); our 32.12 average yields $90.08B, a 0.1% reconciliation gap that is within rounding tolerance.

**Sensitivity.** A ±1% FX move on TWD/KRW reporters changes TSMC external revenue by ±$0.9B, UMC by ±$0.07B, and Samsung Foundry by ±$0.14B — material only for TSMC at the absolute-dollar level.

### Source Tier Legend
- **Tier 1**: Audited 10-K / 20-F / annual report figure with explicit segment footnote.
- **Tier 2**: Derived/estimated from divisional disclosures with management-commentary triangulation.
- **Tier 3**: Third-party analyst data only (not used as primary in this table).

## Q2 — Process Node Maturity: Risk vs HVM Distinction (as of Q1 2026)

**HVM Definition Applied**: ≥10,000 wafers per month (300mm-equivalent) sustained for ≥2 consecutive quarters through Q1 2026. Risk production = engineering wafers and customer-specific tape-outs running below the 10k WPM threshold or with yield not yet qualified for volume customer ramps. Maturity score rubric: 1 = R&D / pathfinding; 2 = pilot line; 3 = risk production / yield-learning; 4 = HVM ramp (qualified, climbing); 5 = mature, high-yield, multi-quarter steady-state.

**Reference baseline for lag**: TSMC N3 family entered qualified HVM in Q1 2023 (per TSMC Q4 2022 earnings call, J. Mark Liu remarks). TSMC N2 entered HVM ramp Q4 2025 (per TSMC Q3 2025 call, C.C. Wei). Lag is computed as **(quarter TSMC's current HVM leading node reached qualified HVM) − (quarter peer's current HVM leading node reached qualified HVM)**, expressed in years to one decimal.

### Narrative — methodology, ND handling, and key judgments

1. **HVM threshold mechanics.** The ≥10k WPM / 2-quarter rule is binding for borderline cases. Three nodes sit ambiguously near the line as of Q1 2026: TSMC N2, Intel 18A, and SMIC's "N+2" 7nm-class. For each, the underlying capacity figure is **not directly disclosed** ("ND"); I triangulated from (a) the count of qualified EUV/DUV scanners installed (per ASML shipment disclosures and SemiAnalysis estimates), (b) management capex commentary, and (c) reported product ramps (Panther Lake at Intel; Apple A20 / NVIDIA Rubin at TSMC; Kirin/Ascend at SMIC). Where my point estimate falls within ±20% of 10k WPM I flagged the node as risk-production rather than HVM.

2. **Samsung yield qualification.** Samsung's SF3 process technically met the WPM definition by Q3 2024, but multiple buy-side teardown reports (TechInsights, SemiAnalysis 2024-2025) and Korean press (KED, BusinessKorea) place SF3 yield 25–40 ppts below TSMC N3 through mid-2025. I therefore down-score SF3 to 3.5 and compute the **effective** lag at ~2.0 years rather than the headline 0-year nominal lag — readers needing the nominal figure should substitute 0.0y.

3. **Lag computation reference.** All lags reference **TSMC N3 family** as TSMC's current sustained HVM leading node; I have **not** treated N2 as TSMC's HVM node because Q1 2026 N2 wafer-out is itself within the threshold uncertainty band (TSMC Q4-2025 call: "N2 capacity ramping ahead of plan, contribution to revenue from 2026"). Using N2 as the reference would compress every lag by ~2.5 years and is less defensible under the 2-quarter sustained rule.

4. **GF, Tower, and Hua Hong** are deliberately non-leading-edge; lag in geometric years is a poor proxy for competitive position because their value is in differentiated platforms (RF-SOI, BCD, eNVM, SiGe). The score 5 reflects mature, high-yield economic position **on their leading node**, not shrink leadership.

5. **Source tiering.** T1 = audited filings (10-K, 20-F, HKEX/KRX annual reports). T2 = management investor presentations, earnings transcripts, technology forums. T3 (not relied on as primary) = third-party teardown / consultant. SMIC's 7nm-class disclosure is the single largest T3-anchored point and is flagged as such.

### Ranking by Capital Efficiency [Revenue × Gross Margin] / CapEx

1. **GlobalFoundries — 2.24** (capex underspend post-2023; runway from Malta + Dresden previously front-loaded)
2. **TSMC — 1.70** (scale + premium ASP on N3/N5 absorbs the world's largest CapEx envelope)
3. **UMC — 0.87** (mature-node depreciation tail short; modest Singapore expansion)
4. **Tower — 0.80** (specialty-analog mix; Intel NMC agreement subsidises cap intensity)
5. **SMIC — 0.20** (China expansion phase: high CapEx, depressed mature-node ASP)
6. **Hua Hong — 0.08** (Wuxi Fab 9 ramp dominates; revenue trough in FY24)
7. **Samsung Foundry — 0.08** (3nm GAA yield drag + aggressive HBM/foundry capex)
8. **Intel Foundry — –0.41** (negative GM, intercompany-priced wafers; pre-18A revenue not yet reflected)

- **Intel Foundry** (CapEx $17B vs IFS-attributable OCF approximated negative)
- **SMIC** ($7.33B vs $3.91B)
- **Hua Hong** ($2.50B vs $0.71B)
- **Tower** (marginal: $0.425B vs $0.39B; counts as ~breakeven)
- **Samsung Foundry** (allocated CapEx $10.5B vs negative segment OCF)

### Methodology Notes & ND Handling

- **Capacity additions (Δ WPM)** are not disclosed uniformly; estimated from (i) issuer fab roadmaps in 2024 annual reports and capital-budget call commentary, (ii) cross-checked with SEMI World Fab Forecast Q1 2026 update. ### Narrative Summary

**Leading-edge concentration is extreme.** Combined ≤7nm capacity across the eight entities sums to ~660k 300mm-eq WPM, of which TSMC controls 43%, Intel Foundry 40%, Samsung 14%, and SMIC ~2% (export-control-bounded). GlobalFoundries, UMC, Tower, and Hua Hong have **zero leading-edge capacity** — a deliberate strategic posture documented in each firm's 20-F/annual report risk-factor sections.

**Revenue-per-wafer dispersion (8.5×).** Intel Foundry's $24.2k/wafer is artificially elevated by internal transfer-priced wafers to Intel Products (a Q1 elimination concern, flagged but not adjusted here per Q4 scope). On an external-only basis, TSMC ($5.3k) leads true commercial pricing power, followed by Samsung Foundry (~$2.4k) and SMIC (~$2.3k). Specialty plays (Tower $1.4k, GFS $0.9k) earn solid mature-node margins; Hua Hong's $0.75k reflects 200mm-heavy mix and Wuxi ramp dilution.

**Utilization classification rationale.** TSMC, Intel (at Intel 3), and SMIC are **capacity-constrained at the leading edge** — TSMC's CoWoS bottleneck (CoWoS capacity is 75k WPM end-2024, doubling to 135k 2025) drives N3/N5 lead-times >30 weeks. Samsung Foundry, UMC, Tower, and Hua Hong are **utilization-constrained** with FY24 loadings of 60%, 67%, ~70%, and ~92% (Wuxi-diluted), respectively — symptomatic of mature-node oversupply post-2023 inventory correction. GlobalFoundries is **balanced** courtesy of its take-or-pay LTA book (>$26B contracted at end-2024 per 10-K p.30).

**As-of-date caveat.** All capacity figures snap to 31-Dec-2024 to align with FY2024 financials per Q4 instructions. Q1'26 capacity (relevant per Q2 HVM definition) would add ~30k WPM at TSMC N3, ~20k at Intel 3 (Fab 34), and ~10k at SMIC N+2.

### Reconciliation notes & limitations

**Bridge balancing rule.** Each row's four components sum (within ±20 bps) to the reported Δ. Where management explicitly quantified one component (e.g., TSMC FX +200 bps), that value is anchored and the depreciation line is the residual plug; this is the most common pattern because issuers disclose FX and depreciation step-up but leave utilization and mix qualitative.

**Samsung Foundry (Entity 2) — segment-only limitation flagged.** Samsung reports DS (Device Solutions) consolidated but does not publish a standalone Foundry segment gross margin in its English 20-F/Business Report. Foundry GM is reconstructed from (a) DS segment operating margin, (b) memory-vs-non-memory revenue split (Note 30 of 2024 Business Report), and (c) sell-side triangulation of Foundry operating losses (~KRW 4–5T in 2024). Confidence: **medium-low**; range disclosed in interval. Normalized 90% utilization GM of 2–8% reflects the gap to TSMC's Foundry-equivalent margin profile after eliminating start-up depreciation.

**Intel Foundry (Entity 3) — segment recast.** The 2024 10-K is the first full year under the recast Intel Foundry / Intel Products segmentation. The Intel Foundry segment reported revenue of ~$17.5B (mostly intercompany) and an operating loss of ~$13.4B; backing out R&D and unallocated costs, segment-level GM is approximately −14% (FY23 pro forma) → −35% (FY24), consistent with management's statements that 2024 was the depreciation-trough year for Intel 4/3 in Fab 34 Ireland. Q3-24 included a $3.1B impairment for tools partially offset later — treated as part of (iv) depreciation step-up to preserve a clean four-component bridge.

**FX treatment.** TWD reporters (TSMC, UMC) used period-average rate; both benefited ~+150–200 bps from TWD weakening (2024 avg 32.50 vs 2023 avg 31.16 per Taiwan Central Bank). KRW reporter (Samsung) used period-average 1,365/USD vs 1,305/USD = ~+150 bps tailwind. RMB reporters (SMIC, Hua Hong) report in USD, so FX effect is small and limited to RMB-denominated cost translation. USD-functional reporters (Intel, GFS, Tower) carry zero FX line in the bridge.

**Depreciation step-up — common driver.** In six of eight names (all except TSMC, where FX dominated, and Tower where the line is small), depreciation step-up is the largest single negative component. This reflects the industry-wide 2023–2024 wave of new 300mm fabs reaching first-silicon and beginning straight-line depreciation: Intel Fab 34 Ireland, GFS Malta module 2, UMC Singapore P3, SMIC Beijing/Lingang/Tianjin, Hua Hong Wuxi Phase II, Samsung Taylor TX. Tower's Agrate Italy 300mm ramp is partly absorbed by ST partnership credits, muting the GM impact.

**Normalized GM @ 90% utilization.** Computed as reported FY24 GM, plus add-back of the (i) utilization component scaled to the gap between actual util and 90%, holding mix/FX/depreciation constant at FY24 levels. This is a steady-state proxy excluding cyclical underload but **including** the higher 2024 depreciation base. Wide intervals reflect ND on actual utilization for Samsung/Intel Foundry segments.

### Allocation methodology details (IDMs)

**Samsung Foundry R&D allocation.** Samsung Electronics reports group-level R&D of **KRW 35.00 trillion** (record high; Business Report 2024, DART filing, p. 87) but does not break out Foundry R&D. Methodology: (i) start with **Device Solutions (DS) R&D ≈ KRW 24.5T** (~$18.0B), which excludes MX/CE/Display; (ii) apply Foundry's share of DS revenue (~24%, since DS = Memory ~KRW 65T + Foundry/SLSI ~KRW 21T); (iii) yield **KRW ~6.0T → ~$4.4B foundry-attributable R&D**. Cross-check vs. Samsung's stated GAA-node and 2nm process-development scope (consistent with industry estimates of $4–5B/yr). Sensitivity band: $3.8–5.0B.

**Intel Foundry R&D allocation.** Intel's restated segment reporting (effective Q1 2024, 10-K p. 51) splits R&D between **Intel Products** and **Intel Foundry**. Reported Intel Foundry operating loss of **$13.4B on $17.5B internal+external revenue** includes a discrete technology-development expense line. Intel does not publish the exact split, but the Foundry-segment expense buildup (Intel 18A, Intel 3, advanced packaging) implies **~$5.2B (≈31% of group R&D)**, with the residual **~$11.3B** in Intel Products (CCG, DCAI, NEX). Confidence: medium — Intel discloses aggregate R&D of $16.546B (10-K p. 73) but the segment cut requires reconstruction.

### Outlier identification (R&D-intensity vs. Q2 node-leadership rank)

The clearest outlier is **Intel Corporation**. Intel's consolidated R&D-to-revenue of **31.2%** is roughly **4× TSMC's 7.1%** and **3× Samsung-group's 11.6%**, yet Intel's HVM-leading node in Q2 (Intel 3, with Intel 18A still in risk production as of Q1 2026) lags TSMC's N3 (≥2 quarters HVM since 2H23) by ~1.5–2 years. Per kWPM of leading-edge capacity, Intel spends **~5.7× TSMC's R&D burden** to achieve a node position that is one full generation behind. The disconnect reflects (a) sub-scale wafer denominator (Intel 4/3 capacity ramping), (b) parallel investment in Intel 18A, 14A, Foveros/EMIB, and PowerVia, and (c) the absence of meaningful external foundry revenue offset (Intel Foundry external rev <$0.5B FY24).

Secondary outlier: **Hua Hong** at 10.5% R&D-intensity with no ≤7nm exposure — but this is structural (specialty/embedded NVM, BCD analog, IGBT) rather than a leadership disconnect; HHGrace's R&D supports specialty-tech differentiation, not node race. Tower at 5.3% sits at the opposite end (efficient specialty model). **TSMC's 7.1% with 280k kWPM ≤7nm capacity is the benchmark** for R&D-leverage efficiency.

| 0.5  | Qualcomm named with reasonable share (8–16%) but pull-in or confidence label missing/imprecise; OR cites consolidated Samsung 10-K equivalent without DART specificity; ±10% band on $ uplift. |
| 0.25 | Recognises Samsung does not disclose a >10% customer but provides no reverse-engineered identity; OR names Qualcomm without any % or sensitivity calc; ND not flagged. |
| 0    | Fabricates Samsung-disclosed customer name as Tier-1 disclosure; wrong customer (e.g., Apple); no citation; ignores intercompany Exynos/SLSI distinction. |

### Intel Foundry (IFS)
| Tier | Condition |
|------|-----------|
| 1.0  | States **>90% intercompany** (Intel Products) as dominant "customer"; external <10% (~$0.75–1B); names Microsoft (18A), DoD RAMP-C, MediaTek as external <10%; 30% pull-in **+27% IFS segment / ~+$4.7B** but flags **no consolidated impact** post-elimination; cites Intel 10-K FY2024 Note 17/19 (Operating Segments). |
| 0.5  | Identifies Intel Products as dominant customer with ≥80% intercompany share; pull-in math within ±10%; missing one external customer name OR misses elimination caveat. |
| 0.25 | Treats IFS as third-party-only (ignores intercompany); OR identifies external customer correctly but pull-in scaled to consolidated Intel rev rather than IFS segment. |
| 0    | Fabricates a >10% external customer; misses intercompany model entirely; no citation. |

### GlobalFoundries
| Tier | Condition |
|------|-----------|
| 1.0  | Top customer ~19% (±3%, range 18.4–19.6%) identified as **Qualcomm** (High confidence) anchored to Apr-14-2024 8-K LTA amendment; AMD residual WSA #2 noted; 30% pull-in **+5.7% / ~+$0.39B** with derivation; cites GFS 10-K FY2024 Note 18 / Item 1A + Qualcomm LTA 8-K. |
| 0.5  | Qualcomm named at 17–21% (±10%); LTA cited but date imprecise; OR pull-in within ±10% of $0.39B but derivation thin. |
| 0.25 | Identifies AMD as #1 (now residual), or names Qualcomm without quantitative %; pull-in not computed. |
| 0    | Wrong identity (e.g., Apple); fabricated >25% concentration; no source. |

### UMC
| Tier | Condition |
|------|-----------|
| 1.0  | Discloses **no single customer >10%** (audit-stated); Top-10 ≈53% noted; reverse-engineers **MediaTek ~9–10%** (Medium confidence) as #1, with Realtek/Novatek/Qualcomm secondary; 30% pull-in **~+2.7% / ~+$0.20B**; cites UMC 20-F FY2024 Item 4.B / TWSE annual report. |
| 0.5  | States no >10% customer correctly; MediaTek named without % anchor OR pull-in within ±10% of +$0.20B; missing one element. |
| 0.25 | Asserts a >10% UMC customer (incorrect); OR no reverse-engineering attempted ("ND, none disclosed"); pull-in absent. |
| 0    | Fabricates a named >10% customer at Tier-1 level; no citation; wrong fundamentals (e.g., claims Apple = 20% of UMC). |

### SMIC
| Tier | Condition |
|------|-----------|
| 1.0  | "Customer A ≈16%" (±3%, range 15.5–16.5%) cited from HKEx 2024 AR Note 4; Top-5 ≈56%; identity flagged **Low–Medium confidence** with both US-fabless (Qualcomm RF) and domestic-Chinese (HiSilicon/UNISOC) hypotheses given export-control opacity; 30% pull-in **+4.8% / ~+$0.39B**. |
| 0.5  | Customer A % within 14–18% (±10%); identity speculation given but confidence level not stated; OR pull-in computed but derivation missing. |
| 0.25 | Customer A % directionally right but materially off; OR names a single high-confidence customer without acknowledging export-control redaction limitation. |
| 0    | Fabricates named customer as Tier-1 fact; no citation; wrong % (e.g., claims ND when 16% is disclosed). |

### Tower Semiconductor
| Tier | Condition |
|------|-----------|
| 1.0  | Largest customer ~22% (±3%, range 21.3–22.7%) identified as **Broadcom/Avago** (High confidence) via RF-SOI process exclusivity logic; #2/#3 at ~14%/~11% noted; 30% pull-in **+6.6% / ~+$0.094B**; cites Tower 20-F FY2024 Item 5.A + Item 3.D risk factor. |
| 0.5  | Broadcom named with share 19.8–24.2% (±10%); pull-in within ±10%; one secondary customer or rationale missing. |
| 0.25 | Identifies a >20% customer but cannot name it / wrong identity; pull-in directionally correct but unscaled. |
| 0    | No top-customer % given; fabricates Apple/NVIDIA as Tower's customer; no citation. |

### Hua Hong Semiconductor
| Tier | Condition |
|------|-----------|
| 1.0  | States **no single customer >10%** disclosed; Top-5 ≈60%; reverse-engineers **STMicroelectronics / Infineon** (Medium confidence on identity, Low on rank-order) as likely top via BCD/IGBT/MCU process partnerships; 30% pull-in **~+2.7% / ~+$0.054B** assuming top single ~9%; cites HKEx 1347 2024 AR Note 5. |
| 0.5  | No >10% customer correctly stated; ST or Infineon named but rank ambiguity not disclosed; OR pull-in within ±10% of +$0.054B but derivation thin. |
| 0.25 | Asserts a >10% customer at HHGrace (incorrect); OR concedes ND without reverse-engineering attempt; pull-in absent. |
| 0    | Fabricates named >10% customer; cites wrong filing (e.g., 10-K — HHGrace files HKEx); no source. |

---

### Cross-Cutting Penalties (Q8-specific)

1. **Citation missing entirely** → cell capped at **0.5** regardless of numeric accuracy. Q8 requires anchoring customer concentration to filings (20-F Item 4.B, 10-K Note 17/18, HKEx Note 4/5, DART business report).
2. **Confidence level not stated** for reverse-engineered identities (Samsung, SMIC, Hua Hong, UMC where identity is inferred) → cell capped at **0.5**. The question explicitly requires "state confidence level (high/medium/low)."
3. **30% pull-in sensitivity not computed** (only customer % given, no FY2025E impact) → cell capped at **0.25**. The pull-in model is a mandatory deliverable.
4. **ND with no reverse-engineering method shown** (i.e., entity says "not disclosed" without attempting design-win allocation logic for Samsung/UMC/HHGrace, or without the redaction caveat for SMIC) → cell capped at **0.25**.
5. **Intercompany elimination ignored for Intel** (treats Intel Products wafers as external "customer concentration" without flagging the elimination effect on consolidated revenue) → Intel cell capped at **0.5**.
6. **Wafer-agreement evidence fabricated** (e.g., inventing an Apple LTA at GFS, a non-existent NVIDIA-Samsung deal) → that cell scores **0** regardless of other elements.
7. **Wrong FX or wrong FY** (uses FY2023 customer concentration or applies FY-end rates to revenue conversion) → −0.25 within the cell, floor at 0.

Note: penalties apply per-cell, not cumulatively across the rubric block; the lowest applicable cap governs.

# Foundry and Semiconductor Manufacturing — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

**Scope note:** FY2024 figures reflect audited annual filings (20-F, 10-K, Business Reports, Annual Reports). Where specific metrics are not disclosed, I estimate with stated methodology and confidence level. All USD conversions noted. Figures rounded; dollar values in millions unless stated.

---

## Q1. External Foundry Revenue — Intercompany Elimination

**FX rates used (period-average FY2024, from company filings / Fed H.10):**
- TWD/USD: 32.12 (TSMC uses reporting TWD; converted at average)
- KRW/USD: 1,364 (Samsung)
- HKD/USD: 7.80 (SMIC/Hua Hong dual HKD/USD reporting; both actually report USD)
- CNY/USD: 7.19 (SMIC subsidiary-level)

| # | Entity | Gross Foundry Rev ($M) | Intercompany Elim ($M) | **External ($M)** | Source |
|---|--------|---------------------:|---------------------:|-----------------:|--------|
| 1 | TSMC | 90,080 | ~0 | **90,080** | 2024 20-F; NT$2,894B ÷ 32.12 |
| 2 | Samsung Foundry | ~17,500 | ~(5,500) | **~12,000** | Est.; not separately disclosed. S.LSI/Exynos wafers eliminated |
| 3 | Intel Foundry | 17,544 | ~(16,500) | **~1,000** | 2024 10-K segment; ~94% internal to Intel Products |
| 4 | GlobalFoundries | 6,750 | 0 | **6,750** | 2024 10-K |
| 5 | UMC | 7,110 | 0 | **7,110** | 2024 20-F; NT$228.3B ÷ 32.12 |
| 6 | SMIC | 8,030 | 0 | **8,030** | 2024 AR (reports USD) |
| 7 | Tower | 1,440 | 0 | **1,440** | 2024 20-F |
| 8 | Hua Hong | 2,004 | 0 | **2,004** | 2024 AR (reports USD) |

**Reconciliation notes:**
- **Intel Foundry**: 2024 segment revenue of $17.5B is ~94% intercompany (Intel Products is its primary customer, with Intel 7 wafers dominant). External foundry revenue (~$1B) is Tower-ramp + legacy + early Intel 18A prepayments.
- **Samsung Foundry**: Not separately reported. DS Division = $66B; Foundry is ~$17–18B gross, of which System LSI (Exynos) and some custom S.LSI captive consumption is ~$5–6B. External ~$12B; confidence **medium**.
- **TSMC/UMC/GFS/SMIC/Tower/Hua Hong**: Pure-plays; external ≈ consolidated.

Rates are **period-average** (appropriate for income-statement translation per IAS 21 / ASC 830).

---

## Q2. Process Node Maturity — Risk vs HVM Distinction

HVM defined as ≥10k WPM sustained ≥2 consecutive quarters (as of Q1 2026 outlook).

| Entity | HVM Leading Node | Risk Production | Maturity (1–5) | Lag vs TSMC (yrs) | Fab |
|--------|------------------|-----------------|:--:|:--:|-----|
| TSMC | **N3 / N3E** (N2 risk) | N2 (H2'25 ramp) | 5 | 0.0 | Fab 18, Tainan |
| Samsung | **3GAE/3GAP** (limited yield) | 2nm SF2 | 3 | ~1.0 | S3 Hwaseong; Taylor TX (delayed) |
| Intel | **Intel 4 / Intel 3** | Intel 18A (risk → HVM late 2025) | 3 | ~1.5 | Fab 34 Leixlip; D1X Oregon |
| GlobalFoundries | **12LP/12LP+** | 12LP+ features | 4 | ~5 (no sub-10nm roadmap) | Fab 8 Malta NY |
| UMC | **22ULP/22ULL** | 14nm (low volume) | 4 | ~6 | Fab 12A Tainan |
| SMIC | **N+1/N+2 (~7nm-class)** | ~5nm-class (export-control limited) | 2 | ~4 | SN1 Shanghai |
| Tower | **65nm RF-SOI / 55nm BCD** | — (specialty focus) | 5 | n/a (specialty) | Migdal Haemek; Uozu JP |
| Hua Hong | **28nm** (limited) | — | 3 | ~7 | HH Fab 7 Wuxi |

Primary sources: TSMC Q4'24 earnings script; Samsung 2024 Business Report; Intel 2024 10-K + Foundry Direct Connect; GFS 10-K; UMC 20-F; SMIC annual report; Tower 20-F; Hua Hong AR.

---

## Q3. CapEx Efficiency — Ratio Decomposition

| Entity | FY24 CapEx ($B) | CapEx/Rev % | $/incremental 300mm-eq wafer | Payback (yrs @ seg EBITDA) | CapEx > OCF? |
|--------|---------------:|:----:|:----:|:----:|:--:|
| TSMC | 29.8 | 33.1% | ~$42k | 2.1 | No |
| Samsung (DS) | ~32 | ~48% | ~$55k | 6+ | **Yes** |
| Intel | 23.9 | 44.9% | ~$80k+ | n/m (neg EBITDA) | **Yes** |
| GFS | 0.7 | 10.4% | low (no adds) | 3.0 | No |
| UMC | 2.9 | 40.8% | ~$35k | 4.1 | No |
| SMIC | 7.3 | 90.9% | ~$30k | 7.5 | **Yes** |
| Tower | 0.35 | 24.3% | modest | 5.0 | No |
| Hua Hong | 2.5 | 124% | ~$28k | 12+ | **Yes** |

**Capital Efficiency Ranking [Rev × GM] / CapEx (higher = better):**

1. **GlobalFoundries** — (6.75 × 0.245)/0.7 ≈ 2.36
2. **TSMC** — (90.1 × 0.561)/29.8 ≈ 1.70
3. **UMC** — (7.11 × 0.336)/2.9 ≈ 0.82
4. **Tower** — (1.44 × 0.232)/0.35 ≈ 0.95
5. **SMIC** — (8.03 × 0.180)/7.3 ≈ 0.20
6. **Samsung Foundry** (est.) — ~0.15
7. **Hua Hong** — (2.00 × 0.105)/2.5 ≈ 0.084
8. **Intel Foundry** — negative (GM negative in 2024)

---

## Q4. Capacity Decomposition by Node Band

Latest-disclosed monthly 300mm-eq installed capacity (as-of dates noted):

| Entity | As-of | Total 300mm-eq WPM (k) | ≤7nm % | 10–28nm % | ≥40nm % | Rev/wafer ($) | Status |
|--------|-------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|--------|
| TSMC | Dec-24 | ~1,600 | ~28% | ~32% | ~40% | $4,690 | **Leading-edge constrained** |
| Samsung Foundry | Dec-24 | ~600 | ~18% | ~35% | ~47% | ~$1,670 (est) | Utilization-constrained |
| Intel Foundry | Dec-24 | ~280 | ~25% (Intel 7/4/3) | ~30% | ~45% | n/m | Utilization-constrained |
| GFS | Dec-24 | ~320 | 0% | ~65% | ~35% | $1,760 | Utilization-constrained |
| UMC | Dec-24 | ~850 (incl 8" eq.) / ~330 300mm | 0% | ~55% | ~45% | ~$1,800 | Utilization-constrained |
| SMIC | Dec-24 | ~950 (8" eq.) / ~400 300mm | ~5% | ~40% | ~55% | ~$1,670 | **Leading-edge constrained** (tool access) |
| Tower | Dec-24 | ~200 (8" eq.) / ~90 300mm | 0 | 0 | 100% | ~$1,350 | Utilization-constrained |
| Hua Hong | Dec-24 | ~390 (8" eq.) / ~140 300mm | 0 | ~40% | ~60% | ~$1,190 | Utilization-constrained |

---

## Q5. Gross Margin Bridge — FY2023 → FY2024

| Entity | FY23 GM | FY24 GM | Δbps | Util | Mix | FX | Depr | Normalized @90% Util |
|--------|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| TSMC | 54.4% | 56.1% | +170 | +150 | +250 | +80 | −310 | ~57–58% |
| Samsung Foundry* | ~neg | ~neg LSD | +300 | +500 | +100 | +50 | −350 | ~5–10% |
| Intel Foundry* | −27% | −76% | −4,900 | −1,200 | flat | flat | **−3,700** | ~−10% (18A ramp cost) |
| GFS | 28.2% | 24.5% | −370 | −400 | +50 | flat | −20 | ~30% |
| UMC | 35.2% | 33.6% | −160 | −250 | +60 | +70 | −40 | ~37% |
| SMIC | 19.3% | 18.0% | −130 | +150 | +80 | flat | −360 | ~22% |
| Tower | 23.4% | 23.2% | −20 | −40 | +30 | flat | −10 | ~26% |
| Hua Hong | 21.3% | 10.5% | −1,080 | −500 | flat | −30 | **−550** | ~17% (post Fab 9 absorption) |

*Samsung Foundry and Intel Foundry segment margins are disclosed only at segment operating-margin level; GM proxies estimated from depreciation + opex disclosures. **Limitation: consolidated-only for Samsung.**

Bridge methodology: variance-analysis using disclosed utilization %, node mix bps (from revenue-by-node tables), FX from hedging disclosures, and new-fab depreciation step-up from PP&E rollforward.

---

## Q6. R&D Allocation and Leading-Edge Intensity

| Entity | R&D ($M) | R&D/Rev % | Foundry-allocated R&D ($M) | R&D/leading-edge wafer ($) |
|--------|---------:|:--:|---------:|---------:|
| TSMC | 6,370 | 7.1% | 6,370 | ~$14,200 |
| Samsung | ~21,500 (total) | ~8% | ~4,500 (foundry; pro-rata on revenue + explicit leading-edge allocation) | ~$41,700 |
| Intel | 16,546 | 31.0% | ~6,500 (Foundry Technology Development segment reclass, 2024) | ~$92,800 |
| GFS | 440 | 6.5% | 440 | n/a (no LE) |
| UMC | 339 | 4.8% | 339 | n/a |
| SMIC | 762 | 9.5% | 762 | ~$38,000 |
| Tower | 54 | 3.8% | 54 | n/a |
| Hua Hong | 160 | 8.0% | 160 | n/a |

**Methodology for IDMs:** Intel 2024 10-K splits "Foundry Technology Development" (~$6.5B) post-segment-reclass; Samsung allocated pro-rata on foundry revenue + incremental GAA 3nm disclosure.

**Leading-edge-R&D ranking (per LE wafer, highest intensity):** Intel » Samsung » SMIC » TSMC.

**Outlier:** **Intel Foundry** — highest R&D-per-LE-wafer by ~6.5× vs TSMC, yet HVM leading-node lag of ~1.5 years. R&D intensity is most disconnected from node-leadership rank (Q2). Secondary outlier: Samsung (high R&D, yield-challenged GAA).

---

## Q7. Headcount and Capital Productivity Ratios

| Entity | Employees | As-of | Source | Rev/employee ($k) | CapEx/eng HC ($k) | HC/capacity σ flag |
|--------|---------:|-------|--------|------:|------:|:--:|
| TSMC | 83,231 | Dec-24 | 20-F | 1,083 | ~640 (58% eng.) | within 1σ |
| Samsung Elec. | 267,800 | Dec-24 | Business Rep. | 1,036 (total) | foundry eng ~25k → ~$1.3M | within 1σ |
| Intel | 108,900 | Dec-24 | 10-K | 489 | ~440 (50% eng.) | **>1σ high HC/capacity** |
| GFS | 13,000 | Dec-24 | 10-K | 519 | 100 | within 1σ |
| UMC | 20,183 | Dec-24 | 20-F | 352 | 215 | within 1σ |
| SMIC | 21,787 | Dec-24 | AR | 369 | 560 | within 1σ |
| Tower | 5,900 | Dec-24 | 20-F | 244 | 103 | **>1σ high HC/capacity** (specialty mix) |
| Hua Hong | 8,400 | Dec-24 | AR | 238 | 510 | within 1σ |

Engineering HC: TSMC discloses ~66% masters+PhD; Intel ~50% engineering; others estimated at 45–60% of total.

**σ-flagged divergences:** Intel (overstaffed relative to 300mm-eq capacity — legacy fab footprint + x86 design bundled); Tower (specialty fabs are headcount-heavy per wafer by design).

---

## Q8. Customer Concentration — Reverse-Engineered Identification

| Entity | Top-1 Customer % | Identity (confidence) | FY25E Impact of +30% pull-in by top customer |
|--------|:--:|-----|:--:|
| TSMC | ~25% | **Apple** (high) | +$6.75B rev; +~7.5% total rev |
| Samsung Foundry | ~20–25% | **Qualcomm/Samsung LSI** (medium) — captive + merchant mix | +~$750M foundry |
| Intel Foundry | >90% | **Intel Products** (high — intercompany) | +~$5B intercompany (non-cash external impact) |
| GFS | ~18% | **Qualcomm** (high — RF/mmWave LTA) | +$365M; +~5.4% rev |
| UMC | ~10–12% | **MediaTek** (high) | +$255M; +~3.6% rev |
| SMIC | ~16% | **Qualcomm via OSAT / domestic IDH** (medium); US restrictions ambiguous | +$385M; +~4.8% rev |
| Tower | ~20% | **Broadcom** (high — RF-SOI/SiGe) | +$86M; +~6.0% rev |
| Hua Hong | ~12% | **STMicro / domestic IDH** (low–medium) | +$72M; +~3.6% rev |

**Reverse-engineering logic:**
- TSMC >10% customers = Apple + NVIDIA (2024 confirmed two customers >10%). Apple historically ~25%, NVIDIA rising from ~11% → ~15% in 2024.
- GFS 10-K discloses Qualcomm as >10% customer.
- Tower: Broadcom & ST historically >10%; Broadcom likely #1.
- UMC: MediaTek dominance in 22/28nm.
- Hua Hong: Most diversified; top-1 likely STMicro or a Chinese IDH (BYD Semi / GigaDevice).

---

### Summary Cross-Reference Matrix

| Dim | Leader | Laggard | Key insight |
|-----|--------|---------|-------------|
| Q1 External Rev | TSMC $90B | Intel Foundry ~$1B | Intel Foundry is >94% captive |
| Q2 Node | TSMC (N3 HVM) | Hua Hong (28nm) | SMIC constrained by tool access |
| Q3 CapEx Efficiency | GFS, TSMC | Intel, Hua Hong | Chinese fabs over-investing pre-revenue |
| Q4 Capacity | TSMC 1.6M WPM | Tower ~90k 300mm-eq | Only TSMC + SMIC leading-edge-constrained |
| Q5 GM | TSMC +170bps | Hua Hong −1,080 bps | Fab-ramp depreciation dominates |
| Q6 R&D | Intel (absolute) / TSMC (effective) | Tower | Intel R&D/wafer is 6.5× TSMC |
| Q7 Productivity | TSMC ($1.08M/emp) | Hua Hong ($238k) | Intel overstaffed per wafer |
| Q8 Concentration | Intel (>90% captive) | Hua Hong (~12% top-1) | TSMC's Apple+NVIDIA = ~40% |

**Confidence legend for estimated figures:** High (TSMC, GFS, UMC, Intel, Tower, Hua Hong, SMIC externally reported); Medium (Samsung Foundry allocations, Hua Hong top-customer identity, Samsung R&D allocation); Low (SMIC effective leading-edge capacity due to export-control opacity).

Q1.rationale: Pure-play USD/native revenue rows are mostly correct, but Samsung and Intel miss the required IDM reconciliation precision. UMC is numerically in range but uses the wrong NT$ revenue base.

Q2.rationale: The answer often identifies the broad node class but misses key HVM-vs-risk distinctions, especially Samsung SF4/SF3 and SMIC 14nm vs 7nm-class. Several maturity scores, lag values, and fab/source details are incomplete or wrong.

Q3.rationale: CapEx headline values are sometimes close, but the derived WPM-cost and payback ratios are frequently wrong. Samsung and Intel use aggregate or consolidated CapEx rather than properly allocated foundry CapEx.

Q4.rationale: Most capacity totals or node-band splits are materially off, with several 8-inch-to-300mm-equivalent conversion problems. Tower is the only row with largely correct specialty-only banding.

Q5.rationale: Reported GM levels are sometimes correct, but most bridges have wrong component signs or magnitudes. UMC is materially wrong, while SMIC is the strongest because it captures the utilization recovery versus depreciation drag.

Q6.rationale: The Intel outlier and leading-edge ranking are directionally correct, but several R&D figures are materially wrong, especially UMC, Tower, and Hua Hong. TSMC's R&D-per-leading-edge-capacity denominator is incorrect.

Q7.rationale: Most disclosed headcounts are close, but CapEx-per-engineering-headcount is widely miscomputed due to unsupported engineering-headcount assumptions. Samsung is not properly foundry-apportioned and Hua Hong uses an out-of-range headcount.

Q8.rationale: TSMC is correct and several identities are directionally reasonable, but Samsung, UMC, and Hua Hong overstate customer concentration or fail the no-single-customer-disclosed caveat. Intel notes intercompany dominance but lacks the full external-customer detail.

# Foundry & Semiconductor Manufacturing — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

**Report Date:** June 2025 | **Reference Period:** FY2024 (CY ending Dec 31, 2024) unless noted | **Currency Base:** USD millions unless stated

> **Methodology Note on FX:** All TWD figures converted at FY2024 period-average rate of **TWD 32.14/USD** (Bloomberg daily average Jan 1–Dec 31, 2024). All KRW figures at **KRW 1,364/USD** (Bank of Korea FY2024 average). All HKD figures at **HKD 7.80/USD** (essentially pegged). Period-end rates (TWD 32.63, KRW 1,472 as of Dec 31, 2024) are noted where firms use them for balance sheet restatement; income statement items use period-average throughout. Sources: Bloomberg FX, respective company filings.

---

## Q1. External Foundry Revenue — Intercompany Elimination

### Methodology
Pure-play foundries (TSMC, GFS, UMC, SMIC, Tower, Hua Hong) have no material intercompany wafer sales; their reported revenue equals external revenue. IDMs with captive foundry services (Samsung, Intel) require segment reconciliation.

---

### Entity-by-Entity Revenue Tables

**1. TSMC (TSM)**

| Line | TWD (bn) | USD (mn) |
|---|---|---|
| Reported net revenue FY2024 | 2,894.3 | 90,072 |
| Intercompany elimination | — | — |
| **External foundry revenue** | **2,894.3** | **90,072** |

TSMC is a pure-play foundry; all revenue is external. FX: TWD 32.14/USD period-average.
*Sources: TSMC 2024 Annual Report, 20-F filed Mar 2025.*

---

**2. Samsung Electronics — Foundry Division**

Samsung consolidates the DS (Device Solutions) segment, which includes Memory, System LSI (design), and Foundry (manufacturing). The foundry unit manufactures wafers sold both externally and to System LSI (Exynos/modem chips).

| Line | KRW (bn) | USD (mn) |
|---|---|---|
| DS Segment total revenue FY2024 | ~97,800 | ~71,700 |
| Memory sub-segment | ~73,500 | ~53,900 |
| System LSI (product design) | ~11,200 | ~8,210 |
| Foundry sub-segment gross revenue (pre-elimination) | ~22,400 | ~16,420 |
| Less: intercompany wafers to System LSI (est.) | ~(8,400) | ~(6,160) |
| **Foundry external revenue (post-elimination)** | **~14,000** | **~10,260** |
| Samsung total consolidated revenue FY2024 | 300,860 | 220,570 |

> **Reconciliation note:** Samsung does not disclose Foundry sub-segment revenue as a standalone line in its annual report. The ~KRW 22.4 trillion gross Foundry figure and ~KRW 8.4 trillion intercompany elimination are derived from: (a) Samsung's disclosed DS operating results, (b) System LSI's estimated ~75% outsource rate to internal foundry, and (c) analyst decompositions from JPMorgan Korea equity research (Feb 2025) and cross-checks vs Samsung DART filing segment footnotes. **Limitation:** Samsung consolidates Foundry + System LSI into one DS reporting sub-unit in its English-language filing. Korean DART filing provides slightly more granularity but still does not publish a standalone foundry P&L. Treat intercompany elimination as an **estimate with ±15% uncertainty range.**

*FX: KRW 1,364/USD period-average. Sources: Samsung 2024 Annual Report, DART filing Mar 2025, JPMorgan Korea semiconductor research.*

---

**3. Intel Corporation — Intel Foundry**

Intel restructured into two reportable segments in early 2024: **Intel Products** (client + data center + network IC design) and **Intel Foundry** (fab + packaging manufacturing services).

| Line | USD (mn) |
|---|---|
| Intel Foundry gross revenue (incl. intercompany) FY2024 | 17,459 |
| Less: intercompany wafering to Intel Products | (13,017) |
| **Intel Foundry external revenue FY2024** | **4,442** |
| Intel Foundry gross revenue FY2023 (restated) | 18,942 |

## Q2. Process Node Maturity — Risk vs HVM Distinction

**HVM Definition applied:** ≥10,000 WPM (wafers per month, 300mm-equivalent) sustained across ≥2 consecutive quarters as of Q1 2026.

**Node Maturity Scale:**
- **1** = R&D / pre-silicon
- **2** = Risk production (<5k WPM, yield <60%)
- **3** = Early HVM ramp (5k–10k WPM, yield 65–75%)
- **4** = Established HVM (>10k WPM, yield 80–90%, multiple customer production)
- **5** = Mature high-yield (>20k WPM, yield >90%, fully depreciated or cost-optimized)

## Key Risk Flags and Analytical Observations

1. **Samsung Foundry structural crisis:** Negative segment gross margin (~–25%), CapEx/Revenue at 93%, and accelerating customer losses to TSMC create an unsustainable financial trajectory without either (a) massive yield improvement at SF3E/SF4 or (b) significant fab utilization from winning back major customers. The Taylor, TX fab sits partially idle.

2. **Intel Foundry breakeven math:** At $4.4B external revenue, Intel Foundry needs approximately **6–7x current external revenue** to reach operating breakeven given its $10.5B CapEx run rate and $5.2B allocated R&D. The path requires winning major HPC/AI foundry contracts on Intel 18A or Intel 14A by 2026–2027.

3. **TSMC's widening moat:** Revenue/wafer of $41,700 vs peers' $3,000–$9,500 reflects pricing power from N3/N5 leadership. N2 HVM entry in Q1 2026 extends this lead. CoWoS advanced packaging creates an additional lock-in moat for AI accelerator customers.

4. **SMIC CapEx paradox:** SMIC's $7.3B CapEx at 91% of revenue represents the most aggressive capacity build in the industry on a relative basis, driven by Chinese government strategic imperatives. However, export restrictions structurally limit this capacity to ≥14nm, creating the risk of a massive mature-node oversupply within China by 2026–2027.

5. **Tower/GFS capital efficiency leaders:** Both companies demonstrate that specialty/mature-node strategies can generate superior capital efficiency despite limited node leadership, serving as models for sustainable foundry economics without leading-edge competition.

### Reconciliation notes

FY2024 revenue of roughly NT$2.894tn converts to about **$90.1bn** using NT$32.11 / US$. TSMC is overwhelmingly an external foundry; no Intel-style intercompany wafer elimination is required.

**Samsung Foundry**  
Samsung Electronics discloses Device Solutions revenue but does not give an audited Samsung Foundry external-revenue line. Foundry sales to Samsung System LSI / Exynos / internal image sensor and logic customers are eliminated at the consolidated level. The table above uses an estimated gross foundry activity base of **$18–19bn**, with **$5–7bn** captive / intercompany, resulting in **$12–13bn external**. This is directionally consistent with market-share data from foundry industry trackers but is not audit-reconcilable from Samsung’s annual report alone.

**Intel Foundry**  
Intel Foundry segment revenue includes manufacturing services provided to Intel Products. The economically relevant external foundry revenue is much smaller, roughly **$0.8–1.0bn** in FY2024. The bulk of the segment revenue is internal wafer manufacturing and packaging support to Intel product groups and is eliminated in consolidation.

---

# Q2. Process node maturity — HVM versus risk production

**Definition applied:** HVM = at least **10k 300mm-equivalent wafer starts per month** sustained for at least two consecutive quarters as of Q1 2026. Because companies do not usually disclose WPM by node, this is assessed from public roadmaps, fab-ramp disclosures, teardown evidence, and customer production activity.

| Entity | Smallest node judged to be in HVM | Risk / pilot node not yet clearly HVM | Maturity score, 1–5 | Lag versus TSMC HVM leading node | Main fab locations | Notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| **TSMC** | **N3 / N3E** clearly HVM; N2 entering early volume / risk-to-ramp | N2 / A16 risk-to-early ramp | **5** | **0 yrs** | Taiwan: Tainan, Hsinchu, Taichung; Arizona ramping N4/N5-class | TSMC is the HVM benchmark. |
| **Samsung Foundry** | **4nm-class** HVM; 3nm GAA technically in production but volume/yield still questioned | SF2 / SF3P / advanced GAA variants | **3–4** | ~1.5–2 yrs | Korea: Hwaseong, Pyeongtaek; Taylor, TX delayed | 3nm GAA is “production,” but not clearly broad, high-yield external HVM. |
| **Intel Foundry** | **Intel 4 / Intel 3** HVM for internal Intel products | 20A cancelled / deemphasized; 18A risk-to-ramp | **3–4** | ~1–2 yrs, depending whether Intel 3 or 18A is benchmarked | Oregon, Arizona, Ireland; Ohio delayed | Intel 18A is strategic but HVM qualification is still customer-dependent. |
| **GlobalFoundries** | **12 / 14nm-class FinFET, 22FDX** HVM | No leading-edge risk node | **4** | ~6–7 yrs | Malta NY, Dresden, Singapore | Specialty / essential-chip focus, not leading-edge. |
| **UMC** | **22 / 28nm** HVM; 14nm exists but not broad leading HVM | 14nm limited / customer-specific | **4** | ~8–9 yrs | Taiwan: Fab 12A, Fab 12i Singapore, Xiamen JV | Deliberately focused on mature / specialty. |
| **SMIC** | **7nm-class / N+1 / N+2** judged limited HVM for domestic customers | 5nm-class development uncertain | **2–3** | ~3–4 yrs | Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen | DUV-only leading-node capability; yield and scale remain opaque. |
| **Tower Semiconductor** | **45–65nm specialty** HVM | No advanced logic risk node | **4** | >10 yrs | Israel, Newport Beach, San Antonio, Japan JV | Analog, RF, power, sensors. |
| **Hua Hong** | **40 / 55nm** HVM; 28nm ramping but not clearly broad HVM | 28nm HKMG / eNVM ramp | **3** | ~10 yrs | Shanghai, Wuxi | Strong embedded NVM / power / MCU base. |

**Interpretation:**  
TSMC is the only entity with mature, very-high-volume **3nm-class** production. Samsung and Intel have credible advanced-node roadmaps, but their HVM status depends heavily on customer mix, yield, and sustained wafer starts. SMIC has demonstrated 7nm-class domestic output, but not with the scale, yield transparency, or EUV tooling base of TSMC / Samsung.

---

# Q3. FY2024 capex efficiency and ratio decomposition

### Capex and efficiency table

Capex per incremental capacity is expressed as **US$000 per added monthly 300mm-equivalent WPM**. This is a modelled metric because node mix and shell/tool timing differ heavily.

| Entity | FY2024 capex | Capex / revenue | Est. incremental 300mm-eq capacity added in FY2024 | Capex per added WPM | Segment EBITDA / cash EBITDA basis | Implied payback | Capex > segment OCF? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **TSMC** | ~$29.8bn | **33.1%** | ~130k WPM | **~$229k/WPM** | ~$58–60bn EBITDA | **~0.5 yrs** | No |
| **Samsung Foundry** | est. ~$8–10bn foundry capex; Samsung semi capex much higher | ~65–75% of external foundry revenue | ~50–70k WPM | **~$130–180k/WPM** | Foundry EBITDA not separately disclosed; likely weak | n.m. | Likely yes for foundry |
| **Intel Foundry / manufacturing** | ~$25bn gross Intel capex | Very high versus external revenue | ~30–50k WPM usable leading/manufacturing capacity | **>$500k/WPM** | Foundry segment EBITDA weak / negative after losses | n.m. | Yes |
| **GFS** | ~$0.6–0.7bn | **~9–10%** | ~5k WPM | **~$120–140k/WPM** | ~$2.2–2.4bn adj. EBITDA | **~0.3 yrs** | No |
| **UMC** | ~$3.0bn | **~41%** | ~20k WPM | **~$150k/WPM** | ~$3.5–3.8bn EBITDA | **~0.8–0.9 yrs** | No / borderline |
| **SMIC** | ~$7.3bn | **~91%** | ~80k WPM | **~$90k/WPM** | ~$4bn EBITDA | **~1.8 yrs** | Yes |

| **Hua Hong** | ~$2.2–2.5bn | **>100%** | ~30–40k WPM | **~$60–75k/WPM** | ~$0.4–0.6bn EBITDA | **~4–5 yrs** | Yes |

### Capital-efficiency ranking

Metric:  
\[
\text{Capital efficiency} = \frac{\text{Revenue} \times \text{Gross margin}}{\text{Capex}}
\]

Approximate ranking:

| Rank | Entity | Comment |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **GFS** | Low capex, solid specialty gross profit. |
| 2 | **TSMC** | Very high capex but extremely high gross profit dollars. |

Revenue per installed wafer can look artificially low for Intel and Samsung because the denominator includes captive / strategic capacity, while the numerator above uses **external foundry revenue**. For TSMC, UMC, GFS, SMIC, Tower, and Hua Hong, the metric is more directly comparable.

---

# Q5. Gross margin bridge, FY2023 → FY2024

The bridge below is a **modelled bps attribution**. Companies generally disclose total gross margin but not a clean quantitative breakdown into utilization, mix, FX, and depreciation.

| **Intel Foundry** | Segment gross margin not cleanly disclosed | Segment gross margin not cleanly disclosed | n.a. | Negative | Neutral / improving | Minor | Strongly negative | n.m.; still structurally challenged |

### Samsung and Intel limitation

* **Samsung** does not disclose a separate Samsung Foundry gross margin. Consolidated Samsung Electronics gross margin is heavily influenced by memory cycle recovery, smartphones, displays, and appliances, so it is not a clean proxy.
* **Intel** discloses Intel Foundry operating loss, but gross margin for the manufacturing/foundry segment is not cleanly separable from restructuring, underutilization, startup depreciation, and internal transfer pricing.

---

# Q6. R&D allocation and leading-edge intensity

### R&D spending

| Entity | FY2024 R&D spending | R&D / revenue | Foundry allocation method |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **TSMC** | ~$6.3–6.4bn | ~7.0% | Direct company R&D. |

| **GFS** | ~$0.45–0.50bn | ~7% | Direct company R&D. |
| **UMC** | ~NT$16bn / **~$0.5bn** | ~7% | Direct company R&D. |

Only companies with meaningful ≤7nm capacity are economically comparable.

| Rank | Entity | Est. ≤7nm WPM | R&D allocated to leading-edge / process | R&D per ≤7nm WPM | Comment |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | **Intel Foundry** | ~250–300k | ~$5–7bn | Very high | Outlier: enormous R&D relative to external foundry revenue and customer scale. |

**Outlier:** **Intel Foundry**. Its R&D intensity is much higher than its external foundry market position and node maturity would imply. Strategically, this reflects a catch-up investment model rather than current foundry revenue economics.

---

# Q7. Headcount and capital productivity

### Employees and productivity

| Entity | Employees, latest annual filing / estimate | As-of date | Revenue used | Revenue / employee | Engineering / R&D headcount basis | Capex / engineering head |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

### Headcount-to-capacity divergence

Using employees per 1k 300mm-equivalent WPM:

| Entity | Employees / 1k WPM | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| **TSMC** | ~58–60 | Highly efficient scale. |
| **Samsung Electronics** | Not meaningful using total Samsung headcount | Foundry-only unavailable. |
| **Intel** | ~130–145 | High; includes IDM product / corporate burden. |

| **UMC** | ~50–55 | Efficient mature-node scale. |

**>1σ divergence flags:**  
* **Intel** is the clear high-side outlier if total headcount is compared with manufacturing capacity.  
* **Samsung** cannot be fairly judged unless Samsung Foundry-only headcount is disclosed.

---

# Q8. Customer concentration and FY2025E pull-in sensitivity

### Largest customer identification

| Entity | FY2024 largest-customer disclosure / estimate | Likely customer identity | Confidence | 30% pull-in impact on FY2025E revenue, holding all else constant |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| **TSMC** | ~22–25% | **Apple** | High | +6.6–7.5% total revenue |
| **Samsung Foundry** | est. 12–18% of external foundry | Qualcomm / NVIDIA / Tesla / internal-adjacent mobile logic mix; no clean disclosure | Low | +3.6–5.4% |
| **Intel Foundry** | External customer concentration very high but revenue small | DoD / packaging customers / early foundry customers; Microsoft / AWS-related commitments are roadmap rather than FY2024 revenue | Low | Small in Intel total revenue; potentially +20–30% of external foundry revenue |
| **GFS** | Largest customer likely low-to-mid teens | **AMD** historically, also Qualcomm / NXP / automotive accounts | Medium | +3–5% |
| **UMC** | No dominant >10% customer publicly clear | MediaTek / Novatek / Qualcomm / TI-like broad mix | Low / medium | +2–3% |
| **SMIC** | est. 10–20% | **Huawei / HiSilicon ecosystem** likely meaningful after China localization | Medium | +3–6% |
| **Tower** | Top-10 meaningful; largest likely around 10–12% | Analog / RF / imaging customer; possible ST, Panasonic/TPSCo-linked, or large analog IDMs | Low | +3–4% |
| **Hua Hong** | Largest likely <10% or low teens | China MCU / power / eNVM customers; identity not cleanly disclosed | Low | +2–3% |

### Pull-in model

If the top customer represents \( X\% \) of FY2024 revenue and pulls in orders by 30%, with all other revenue constant:

\[
\text{Revenue uplift} = 0.30 \times X\%
\]

| Entity | External revenue base | Assumed top-customer share | Revenue impact from 30% pull-in |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **TSMC** | ~$90.1bn | 23% | **~+$6.2bn** |
| **Samsung Foundry** | ~$12.5bn | 15% | **~+$0.6bn** |

| **GFS** | ~$6.75bn | 14% | **~+$0.28bn** |
| **UMC** | ~$7.23bn | 9% | **~+$0.20bn** |
| **SMIC** | ~$8.03bn | 15% | **~+$0.36bn** |
| **Tower** | ~$1.44bn | 11% | **~+$0.05bn** |
| **Hua Hong** | ~$2.0bn | 9% | **~+$0.05bn** |

---

# Overall synthesis

## Strategic position by company

| Entity | Positioning summary |
|---|---|
| **TSMC** | Dominant external foundry; best combination of scale, leading-node maturity, gross margin, and R&D efficiency. Capacity tightness is concentrated at N3 / advanced packaging / AI-related flows. |
| **Samsung Foundry** | Technologically ambitious but commercially challenged by utilization, yield perception, and customer concentration volatility. 3nm GAA leadership claims have not translated into TSMC-like external HVM scale. |
| **Intel Foundry** | Strategic turnaround option, not yet an economically scaled external foundry. External revenue is tiny relative to manufacturing capex and process R&D. |
| **GlobalFoundries** | Capital-disciplined specialty foundry with strong efficiency; not competing at leading edge. |
| **UMC** | Mature-node scale operator with good profitability but cyclical utilization pressure. |
| **SMIC** | China-localization beneficiary; capex-heavy, geopolitically constrained, but strategically important. Leading-node progress is real but opaque and less efficient. |
| **Tower** | Specialty analog / RF / sensor foundry with modest capex and niche value, but lower scale. |
| **Hua Hong** | China mature-node / embedded NVM / power foundry; near-term margins pressured by 12-inch ramp depreciation and utilization. |

## Most important comparative findings

1. **External revenue leadership:** TSMC remains vastly larger than every other external foundry.  
2. **Intercompany elimination matters most for Intel and Samsung:** Intel’s foundry segment is mostly internal; Samsung’s internal SLSI demand materially obscures the external foundry picture.  
3. **Node maturity leadership:** TSMC’s N3 HVM scale is unmatched. Samsung and Intel have credible advanced nodes, but HVM economics remain unproven versus TSMC.  
4. **Capital efficiency:** GFS and TSMC screen best; Intel Foundry and Hua Hong screen weakest because capex is far ahead of current earnings power.  
5. **R&D outlier:** Intel is the clearest outlier — extremely high R&D intensity relative to current external foundry share.  
6. **Customer concentration:** TSMC’s largest customer is almost certainly Apple; SMIC’s most strategically important customer is likely Huawei / HiSilicon-related; others are less transparent.

Q1.rationale: Most revenue figures are directionally close and FX conventions are stated, but entity-level filing citations and precise IDM reconciliations are largely absent. Intel and Samsung are handled with reasonable uncertainty but not to full rubric specificity.

Q2.rationale: The answer distinguishes HVM and risk production in broad terms, but lacks citations and often misses the reference node/lag details. SMIC incorrectly treats 7nm-class as limited HVM, and UMC/Tower/Hua Hong lags or nodes are materially off.

Q3.rationale: TSMC is mostly correct except for the capacity-addition denominator and missing citations. Most other rows have materially wrong capex-per-WPM, payback, EBITDA, or ranking details, and Intel uses consolidated capex without a proper foundry allocation.

Q4.rationale: The answer gives a capacity table, but several totals and node-band splits are materially wrong, especially TSMC, Samsung, GFS, Tower, and Hua Hong. SMIC is closest on total capacity and leading-edge caveat, but still lacks source-tier detail.

Q5.rationale: The bridge is explicitly modelled but many component signs and bps values do not reconcile to reference values. Samsung and Intel flag disclosure limitations but do not provide the required reconstructed segment bridge.

Q6.rationale: Intel is correctly identified as the outlier, but the leading-edge capacity denominators and ranking are wrong, and several R&D figures are materially off. IDM allocation methods are vague and citations/page anchors are missing.

Q7.rationale: Headcount ranges are often directionally plausible, but engineering-headcount denominators and capex-per-engineer ratios are mostly inconsistent with the rubric. Intel gets partial credit for the correct consolidated headcount and outlier flag.

Q8.rationale: TSMC, Samsung, UMC, and Hua Hong are directionally reasonable on concentration and pull-in math, though citations are absent. Intel misses the intercompany-customer framing, GFS names AMD rather than Qualcomm, SMIC overstates confidence in Huawei, and Tower misses the Broadcom/22% disclosure.

**Foundry and Semiconductor Manufacturing — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)**

---

### Preamble: Data Vintage & Scope Limitations
*Analysis Date: April 2024 (Model Knowledge Cutoff)*  
*Data Status: FY2024 full-year actuals are not yet finalized / publicly filed for most calendar-year reporters as of this cutoff. Q1 2026 forward data is inherently projection-based. The analysis below provides (1) rigorous **Methodology & Governing Equations** for each dimension, and (2) **Best-Available Population** using the latest reported actuals (primarily FY2023/4Q23 and, where available, 1Q24–2Q24 YTD filings), clearly date-stamped. All forward-looking node classifications (Q2) are derived from disclosed roadmaps and ramp schedules as of the knowledge cutoff.*

---

## Q1. External Foundry Revenue — Intercompany Elimination

### Methodology & Governing Equations
External Foundry Revenue = Gross Foundry / Wafer-Fabrication Revenue − Intercompany Wafer Sales − Packaging / Test / Materials Revenues (non-wafer).

**Intercompany Elimination Rules by Entity:**

| # | Entity | Intercompany Elimination Methodology | FX Convention |
|---|--------|--------------------------------------|---------------|
| 1 | **TSMC (TSM)** | Intercompany sales are negligible (<1%). Consolidated revenue ≈ External Foundry Revenue. Use as-is. | TWD/USD: Use **period-average** rate per company’s consolidated income statement (historically ~30.3–32.0 range; apply exact FY2024 weighted-average when disclosed). |
| 2 | **Samsung (005930.KS)** | Foundry is embedded in Device Solutions (DS) → Semiconductor → Foundry. Eliminate internal wafer shipments to Samsung System LSI (mobile Exynos, modem, image sensors) and Samsung Display (DDIC). Use Samsung’s separate “Foundry” external revenue disclosure if provided; otherwise derive: *DS Semiconductor Revenue − Memory − System LSI external − Inter-DS transfers*. | KRW/USD: Use **period-average** rate from Samsung’s consolidated statements (historically ~1,250–1,330 KRW/USD; apply exact FY2024 avg). |
| 3 | **Intel (INTC)** | Since 1Q24, Intel reports **Intel Foundry (IF)** and **Intel Products (IP)** as separate operating segments. Intercompany eliminations are explicitly disclosed in the “Other” / reconciliation column. External Foundry Revenue = IF Gross Revenue − Intercompany Revenue to Intel Products (primarily wafer sales + packaging). | USD (reporting currency). |
| 4 | **GlobalFoundries (GFS)** | Pure-play foundry; minimal intercompany. Consolidated wafer revenue ≈ External. | USD. |
| 5 | **UMC (UMC)** | Pure-play; external only. | TWD/USD, **period-average**. |
| 6 | **SMIC (0981.HK)** | Pure-play; external only. Note: Historical Huawei/HiSilicon revenues are external but subject to export-control reclassification. | HKD/USD, **period-average** (or RMB via HKD reporting). |
| 7 | **Tower (TSEM)** | Pure-play; external only. | USD. |
| 8 | **Hua Hong (1347.HK)** | Pure-play; external only. | HKD/USD, **period-average** (RMB functional). |

### Best-Available Population (External Foundry Revenue)
*Note: FY2024 actuals pending Q4 filings. Below figures are FY2023 Actuals as baseline; apply FY2024 node ramps (N3 for TSMC, 18A for Intel, etc.) to scale.*

| Entity | FY2023 Actual External Foundry Rev (USD M) | FY2024 Directional Guidance / Framework |
|--------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| TSMC | ~$69,300 | N3 volume ramp; guided high-20s % USD growth for full-year 2024. |
| Samsung (Foundry ext.) | ~$8,500–9,500 (estimated by sell-side; Samsung does not cleanly split external vs. S.LSI) | Flat-to-slight growth; 3nm GAA yield recovery vs. internal Exynos demand. |
| Intel (IF ext.) | ~$100–200 (negligible external in FY2023) | Expect step-up in 2H24 with pan-European / U.S. government anchor customers; still <5% of IF total. |
| GlobalFoundries | ~$7,400 | Guided flat-to-low-single-digit decline in 2024 on macro / automotive digestion. |
| UMC | ~$6,000 | Utilization-driven; modest rebound in 2H24. |
| SMIC | ~$6,300 | Revenue growth expected on China domestic demand and mature-node pricing. |
| Tower | ~$1,400 | acquisition by Intel terminated; organic growth in RF/SiGe. |
| Hua Hong | ~$2,200 (8” + 12”) | Mature-node capacity expansion in Wuxi / Hefei; pricing pressure. |

**Reconciliation Protocol (Pre- vs. Post-Elimination):**
- **Intel**: Pre-elimination IF revenue was ~$18–19B in FY2023 (including intercompany wafers for Client + Data Center). Post-elimination external is <1% of that. Monitor 10-K segment footnote “Intercompany eliminations” to reconcile to the ~$18B segment total.
- **Samsung**: DS Semiconductor revenue was ~$65B in FY2023. Memory is ~70% of DS. Remaining ~$15–20B is System LSI + Foundry. External foundry is estimated by subtracting known internal S.LSI wafer demand (Exynos, ISOCELL, display drivers).

---

## Q2. Process Node Maturity — Risk vs HVM Distinction

### Definition Lock
- **HVM**: ≥10k WPM (300mm-equivalent) sustained for ≥2 consecutive quarters as of **Q1 2026** (implying qualification completed by mid-2025).
- **Risk Production**: Silicon proven, yield learning ongoing, shipments accepted for early customer qualification but <10k WPM or not yet sustained for 2 quarters.
- **Score**: 1=R&D/Pathfinding; 2=Risk/Yield Learning; 3=Early HVM (1–10k WPM); 4=HVM Ramp (10k+ WPM, 70–85% yield); 5=Mature High-Yield (>85% yield, >6 quarters in HVM).

### Node Maturity Matrix & TSMC Lag Calculation

| Firm | HVM Leading Node (Q1 2026E) | Risk Node (Q1 2026E) | Maturity Score | Fab Location(s) | Lag Behind TSMC (Years) | Primary Disclosure Source |
|------|-----------------------------|----------------------|----------------|-----------------|-------------------------|---------------------------|
| **TSMC** | **N2 (2nm)** – early HVM by Q1 2026 (GigaFab 20/21, Hsinchu/Baoshan) | A16 (1.6nm) risk | 3→4 (N2 ramping) | Hsinchu, Taichung (Baoshan), Kaohsiung | 0 (baseline) | Q4 2023 / 2024 Analyst Day; A. Liu commentary |
| **Samsung** | **3nm GAA SF3** (sustained HVM if yield fixes hold; Line 3, Pyeongtaek) | **2nm GAA** risk (2025–2026) | 3 (3nm HVM but yield-constrained) | Pyeongtaek S5 | **2.5–3.0 years** (lag to N2; lag to N3 was ~1.5 yr) | Samsung DS IR; Tech Day 2023 |
| **Intel** | **18A** (scheduled HVM 2H 2025; Oregon + Ireland) | **14A** risk | 3 (18A early HVM by Q1 2026 if roadmap holds) | D1X (Oregon), Fabs 34/35 (Ireland) | **2.0–2.5 years** (18A ≈ TSMC N3.5; N2 is 2025 for TSMC) | Intel 2023–2024 Foundry Direct; 10-K segment risk factors |

| **UMC** | **14nm** (limited HVM); **28nm is true revenue-leading HVM** | 14nm expansion | 4 (28nm mature); 3 (14nm niche) | Tainan (Fab 12A/B), Singapore | **8+ years** | UMC 2023 AR; 28nm is peak revenue node |
| **SMIC** | **7nm (N+2)** low-volume HVM (DUV multi-patterning); **14nm is safer HVM call** | 5nm risk (if equipment access exists) | 2–3 (7nm yield-constrained / sanctions-limited); 4 (14nm) | Shanghai (SN1, SN2), Beijing, Shenzhen | **5–6 years** (7nm vs N2; 3–4 years vs N3) | SMIC 2023 20-F; Equipment disclosure |
| **Tower** | **65nm / 40nm** RF CMOS / Power (HVM) | 22nm niche RF | 5 (mature specialty) | Migdal HaEmek (Israel), Newport Beach (U.S.), San Antonio (U.S.) | **10+ years** (specialty analog) | Tower 2023 20-F; Panasonic JV |
| **Hua Hong** | **90nm / 55nm** BCD / eNVM (HVM); **40nm limited** | 40nm expansion | 5 (mature / power analog) | Wuxi (12”), Shanghai (8”) | **10+ years** | Hua Hong 2023 Annual Report |

**Qualitative Classification:**
- **Capacity-constrained at leading edge**: TSMC (N3/N2 CoWoS demand > supply), Intel (18A capacity limited by EUV tool availability), SMIC (7nm constrained by lithography access).
- **Utilization-constrained**: GlobalFoundries, UMC, Tower, Hua Hong (mature-node utilization in 70–80% range during FY2024 cyclical trough).
- **Balanced**: Samsung (foundry utilization low due to internal/external mix shifts).

---

## Q3. CapEx Efficiency — Ratio Decomposition

### Methodology
**(a)** CapEx % of Revenue = Total CapEx / Total Revenue × 100  
**(b)** CapEx per Incremental 300mm-Equivalent Wafer = CapEx / (Δ WPM × 12 months). Δ WPM derived from disclosed year-end capacity minus prior year-end capacity, converted to 300mm-equivalent using 2.25× multiplier for 200mm where applicable.  
**(c)** Implied Payback (Years) = CapEx / Segment EBITDA.  
**Ranking Metric**: Capital Efficiency = (Revenue × Gross Margin) / CapEx. Higher = better.

### FY2024 CapEx Framework & FY2023 Baseline
*Note: FY2024 CapEx guidance was issued by most firms by early 2024; actuals will be reported in 1Q25 filings.*

| Entity | FY2023 CapEx (USD B) | FY2024 CapEx Guidance (USD B) | FY2024 CapEx > OpCF? | Capital Efficiency Rank (FY2023 Baseline) |
|--------|----------------------|-------------------------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| TSMC | ~$30.4 | Guided ~$28–32B (N2 build-out) | Yes (OpCF ~$38B, but >60% converted to CapEx) | **1** (Highest: massive rev × GM / CapEx) |
| Samsung (DS total) | ~$40+ (total DS; foundry portion est. 25–30%) | Guided similar or slightly lower; foundry share rising | Yes | **3** (efficient but lower GM than TSMC) |
| Intel (total) | ~$25.0 | Guided stepped up for 18A/20A Fabs | **Yes** (Foundry FCF deeply negative) | **7** (lowest external revenue, highest burden) |
| GlobalFoundries | ~$1.2 | Guided ~$1.0B (maintenance/light expand) | No (OpCF > CapEx) | **2** (high margin on low CapEx base) |
| UMC | ~$3.0 | Guided moderation; 28nm/22nm specialty | No | **4** |
| SMIC | ~$7.0+ | Elevated (Beijing/Shenzhen 12” fabs) | **Yes** (heavy state-supported CapEx) | **6** (low margin, high CapEx) |
| Tower | ~$0.4 | Maintenance | No | **5** |
| Hua Hong | ~$1.5+ | Wuxi Fab expansion | Yes (funding via IPO proceeds) | **8** (lowest GM, heavy CapEx) |

**Ratio Decomposition (Illustrative FY2023 Math for TSMC):**
- (a) CapEx % Rev: $30.4B / $69.3B = **43.9%**
- (b) CapEx per incremental wafer: TSMC added ~N3 60k WPM net 300mm-equiv in 2023. $30.4B / (60k × 12) = ~$42k per wafer. *Note: Exact incremental WPM is proprietary; use disclosed year-end capacity changes.*
- (c) Payback: $30.4B / ~$40B EBITDA ≈ **0.8 years** (exceptional).

---

## Q4. Capacity Decomposition by Node Band

### Capacity Band Definitions
- **Leading-Edge (LE)**: ≤7nm (N7, N5, N3, N2 for logic; 7nm/5nm equivalent for SMIC).
- **Middle**: 10nm–28nm (N10/N12/N16/N20/N22/N28).
- **Mature**: ≥40nm / Specialty / 200mm analog.

### Capacity & Utilization Framework
*Note: Exact WPM is competitively sensitive. Below are **directional industry consensus estimates** as of late 2023 / early 2024, subject to Q1 2025 filing updates.*

| Entity | LE ≤7nm WPM (300mm-eq) | Middle 10–28nm WPM | Mature ≥40nm / 200mm WPM | FY2024 Utilization Disclosure | Constraint Classification | Capacity Date |
|--------|------------------------|--------------------|--------------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------------|---------------|

| Samsung (Foundry) | ~20k–30k (3nm GAA; low yield) | ~60k (5nm/7nm) | ~150k+ (28nm–130nm, incl. 200mm) | Foundry utilization ~50–60% in 1H24 (internal mix) | **Utilization-constrained** | 1Q24 |
| Intel (Foundry) | Negligible external LE; 18A coming | ~20k (Intel 7/4) | ~100k+ (legacy 14nm/22nm, 200mm) | IF utilization <50% (ramp phase) | **Utilization-constrained** | 1Q24 |
| GlobalFoundries | 0 (cap at 12nm) | ~30k (12nm/14nm/22FDX) | ~250k+ (28nm–180nm, 200mm, SiGe) | ~70% in 1Q24 | **Utilization-constrained** | 4Q23 |
| UMC | 0 (cap at 14nm niche) | ~80k (14nm/22nm/28nm) | ~250k+ (40nm–350nm, 200mm) | ~70% in 1Q24 | **Utilization-constrained** | 4Q23 |

| Tower | 0 | 0 | ~50k+ (65nm–1µm, heavy 200mm RF/power) | ~70–75% | **Utilization-constrained** | 4Q23 |
| Hua Hong | 0 | ~10k (40nm/55nm) | ~200k+ (90nm–1µm, 200mm dominant) | ~85–90% (local demand) | **Balanced** | 4Q23 |

- TSMC: ~$6,500–7,500 (blended; N3 > $15k, mature ~$2k)
- Samsung: ~$4,000–5,000 (blended external)
- Intel: ~$5,000–6,000 (blended, mostly internal transfer pricing)
- GF: ~$2,500–3,000
- UMC: ~$2,000–2,500
- SMIC: ~$1,800–2,200
- Tower: ~$2,000–2,800 (specialty ASP premium)
- Hua Hong: ~$1,000–1,500 (power/ analog)

---

## Q5. Gross Margin Bridge — FY2023 → FY2024

### Methodology
Bridge components must sum to total bps Δ in GAAP Gross Margin:
**(i) Utilization Effect**: Δ Utilization % × Fixed Cost Coverage (depreciation + labor + utilities) ≈ (New Util − Old Util) × Fixed Cost / Revenue.  
**(ii) Mix Shift**: Revenue-weighted Δ in node GM (e.g., N3 ramp adds +300–500 bps at TSMC if N3 GM > corporate avg).  
**(iii) FX**: Non-USD reporters (TSMC, UMC, SMIC, Hua Hong) translate COGS in TWD/RMB/HKD vs. USD revenue. TWD depreciation vs. USD is margin-accretive for TSMC/UMC.  
**(iv) Depreciation Step-Up**: New fab ramps (N3, 18A) add undepreciated COGS before revenue yield catches up. Typically **−100 to −300 bps** during the first 12–18 months of a node ramp.

### Bridge Framework by Firm
*Data Status: Full FY2024 actuals pending. Below is **hypothetical bridge architecture** using known directional vectors from 1H24.*

| Firm | FY2023 GM | FY2024E GM Direction | (i) Utilization | (ii) Mix Shift | (iii) FX | (iv) Depreciation Step-Up | Normalized GM @ 90% Util |
|------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------------|----------|---------------------------|--------------------------|

| Samsung (Foundry) | ~15–20% (consolidated DS margin higher; foundry lower) | Flat to −200 bps | −100 bps (low utilization) | 0 (no node leap) | 0 (KRW neutral) | −100 bps (Pyeongtaek S5 shell) | ~25–30%* |
| Intel (IF) | Deeply negative (internal transfers) | Still negative; narrowing | +100 bps (loading) | +50 bps (advanced packaging) | N/A (USD) | −500 bps (18A/N2 tool depreciation) | ~20–25%* (long-term target, not near-term) |
| GlobalFoundries | 28.4% | −100 to +50 bps | +100 bps (rebound) | −50 bps (automotive pricing down) | N/A | −50 bps (Malta expansion) | ~32–34% |
| UMC | 35.0% | +100 to +200 bps | +150 bps (utilization up) | −50 bps (28nm pricing pressure) | −50 bps (TWD) | −50 bps | ~38–40% |
| SMIC | 19–21% | Flat to +100 bps | +50 bps | −50 bps (mature ASP down) | −50 bps (RMB) | +50 bps (scale) | ~25–28% |
| Tower | 25–27% | +100 bps | +100 bps (RF demand) | 0 | N/A (USD) | 0 | ~30% |
| Hua Hong | 15–18% | −50 to +50 bps | 0 (already high) | 0 | −50 bps (RMB) | 0 | ~20% |

*\*Intel and Samsung use consolidated or segment proxies. Intel Foundry segment GM is not independently comparable to pure-play foundries because intercompany transfer pricing distorts both revenue and COGS. Samsung does not disclose pure foundry GM.*

---

## Q6. R&D Allocation and Leading-Edge Intensity

### Methodology
- **IDM Allocation (Intel, Samsung)**: Split R&D using segment P&L disclosures. If not fully split, allocate by headcount or by management’s stated “external vs. internal” technology development ratio. Intel is moving to full segment split in 2024; Samsung uses consolidated DS R&D with memory dominating.
- **R&D-per-LE-Wafer** = Total R&D / (LE ≤7nm WPM × 12).

### R&D Framework

| Entity | FY2023 R&D (USD M) | FY2023 R&D % Rev | LE Capacity (Q4) | R&D/LE Wafer (USD) | Allocation Methodology (IDMs) | Rank by R&D/LE Wafer |
|--------|--------------------|------------------|--------------------|--------------------|------------------------------|----------------------|
| TSMC | ~$5,800 | ~8.4% | ~120k WPM | ~$4,000 | N/A (pure-play) | 2 |
| Samsung (DS est.) | ~$15,000+ (total DS) | ~12% (DS) | ~25k WPM | ~$50,000+ | **High uncertainty**: Allocate 30–40% of DS R&D to foundry logic (remainder to memory/V-NAND). Samsung does not disclose pure foundry R&D. | 1 (highest) |
| Intel (total) | ~$16,000 | ~28% | Negligible external LE | N/A (denominator near zero) | Since 1Q24, Intel reports “Intel Foundry” R&D separately; vast majority of process R&D sits in IF to serve both external and internal. | N/A (external denominator = ~0) |
| GlobalFoundries | ~$1,100 | ~15% | 0 | N/A (no LE capacity) | N/A | N/A |
| UMC | ~$600 | ~10% | ~5k (14nm niche) | ~$10,000 | N/A | 4 |
| SMIC | ~$1,200+ | ~19% | ~5k–10k | ~$10,000–20,000 | N/A | 3 |
| Tower | ~$120 | ~8.5% | 0 | N/A | N/A | N/A |
| Hua Hong | ~$150 | ~7% | 0 | N/A | N/A | N/A |

### Outlier Identification
**Intel** is the critical outlier: Its R&D intensity (as % of revenue) is the highest in the peer set (~28%), and its node leadership (18A coming in 2025) is **disconnected** from its effective external foundry scale (near-zero ≤7nm external wafers in FY2024). By the Q2 maturity score, Intel is mid-tier (18A ≈ N3.5), yet its R$/wafer spent on leading-edge development is effectively infinite because it has no external LE volume. This reflects its IDM model, not pure-play efficiency.

---

## Q7. Headcount and Capital Productivity Ratios

### Methodology
- Revenue-per-Employee = Revenue / Total Employees.
- CapEx-per-Engineering-Headcount = CapEx / (Total Employees × Engineering %). Engineering % derived from R&D headcount disclosures or stated technical workforce mix.

### Headcount Framework (Latest Available)

| Entity | Total Employees (As-of Date) | Revenue/Employee (USD) | Eng. Headcount (Est.) | CapEx/Eng Headcount (USD) | Headcount/Capacity Ratio (σ Divergence) |
|--------|------------------------------|------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| TSMC | ~73,000 (Dec 2023) | ~$949,000 | ~20,000 R&D + ~15,000 manufacturing engineers | ~$850,000 | **Baseline** |
| Samsung (DS total) | ~74,000 (DS, Dec 2023) | ~$877,000 (DS avg; foundry lower) | ~25,000+ engineers | ~$1,200,000+ | +0.5σ (DS total vs. foundry-only skews this) |
| Intel | ~120,000 (Dec 2023) | ~$542,000 | ~50,000+ engineers | ~$500,000 | **+1.2σ** (high headcount vs. capacity; IDM/product design bloat) |
| GlobalFoundries | ~13,000 (Dec 2023) | ~$569,000 | ~2,500 R&D + Mfg Eng | ~$480,000 | −0.3σ |
| UMC | ~20,000 (Dec 2023) | ~$300,000 | ~3,000 engineers | ~$1,000,000 | −0.1σ |
| SMIC | ~20,000+ (Dec 2023) | ~$315,000 | ~4,000 engineers | ~$1,750,000 | +0.8σ (heavy CapEx/eng on 12” expansion) |
